text:
Predicates:
RankedHighly(x) ::: x is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
ActivePlayer(x) ::: x is one of the most active players in major tennis.
LostTo(x, y) ::: x lost to y.
Female(x) ::: x is a female tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
Male(x) ::: x is a male tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
PlayerAtRG2022(x) ::: x is a tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
AtRG2022(x) ::: x is at Roland Garros 2022.

Premises:
∀x (RankedHighly(x) → ActivePlayer(x)) ::: If someone is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association, then they are one of the most active players in major tennis.
∀x (LostTo(x, iga) → RankedHighly(x)) ::: Everyone who lost to Iga Świątek at Roland Garros 2022 is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
∀x (Female(x) ∧ PlayerAtRG2022(x) → LostTo(x, iga)) ::: All female tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Iga Świątek.
∀x (PlayerAtRG2022(x) → (Female(x) ∨ Male(x))) ::: All tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 are either female or male.
∀x (Male(x) ∧ PlayerAtRG2022(x) → LostTo(x, rafael)) ::: All male tennis players at Roland Garros in 2022 lost to Rafael Nadal.
(RankedHighly(coco) ∨ LostTo(coco, rafael)) → ¬(Male(coco) ∧ PlayerAtRG2022(coco)) ::: If Coco Gauff is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association or lost to Rafael Nadal, then Coco Gauff is not a male tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
AtRG2022(coco) ::: Coco Gauff is at Roland Garros 2022.

Conclusion:
ActivePlayer(coco) ::: Coco Gauff is among the most active major tennis players.
